title: Pant's Wellington 128 Makes Him First Asian Keeper With Hundreds in All SENA Countries
excerpt: Rishabh Pant's ninth Test century, reached with a six off Glenn Phillips, completed a set only two other wicketkeepers in history hold — and made him the sixth Indian batter with hundreds in South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
body:
• Rishabh Pant's 128 off 153 balls against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve made him the first Asian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries.
  • He is the sixth Indian batter to complete the set, joining Azharuddin, Tendulkar, Dravid, Kohli and KL Rahul — who did it a day earlier in the same match.
  • It was Pant's ninth Test hundred as a designated wicketkeeper, third on the all-time list behind Adam Gilchrist (17) and Andy Flower (12).
  • Pant reached his hundred off 135 balls with a six off Glenn Phillips, and his six sixes took him to 108 Test sixes, past Brendon McCullum's 107 and second only to Ben Stokes (138).

Rishabh Pant completed a set no Asian wicketkeeper had managed before him. His 128 off 153 balls against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Sunday gave him Test centuries in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia — and made him the first Asian wicketkeeper, and the first visiting wicketkeeper, to do it, as MyKhel reported.

How the hundred was made

Pant, 29 and returning to the side for the first time since the Sri Lanka tour in August, reached three figures off 135 deliveries in the manner that has become his signature: a reverse sweep off Glenn Phillips took him to 99, and a slog over mid-off for six brought up the hundred — the fourth time in his Test career he has reached a century with a six. He hit 10 fours and six sixes in all before left-arm spinner Rachin Ravindra dismissed him for 128 shortly before lunch on the fourth day, with India extending their lead to 261 runs by the interval, according to Madhyamam. India went on to declare at 720 for 9.

The company he now keeps

Among Indian batters, Pant is the sixth to score Test hundreds in each SENA country, after Mohammad Azharuddin, Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul. Rahul had become the fifth — and the first Indian opener — only a day earlier in this same Wellington innings, so the list grew by two names in one match. Among wicketkeepers worldwide, Pant joins Adam Gilchrist and Jonny Bairstow as the third to complete the SENA set. His nine centuries as a designated wicketkeeper place him third on that all-time list, behind Gilchrist's 17 and Andy Flower's 12.

Eight years of away hundreds

The set was eight years in the making. Pant's first SENA hundred was 114 at The Oval in 2018, followed by an unbeaten 159 against Australia in Sydney in 2019 and an unbeaten 100 against South Africa in Cape Town in 2022. He added 146 against England at Birmingham later in 2022 and two more centuries against England at Leeds in 2025. Wellington was the missing piece — and, Madhyamam noted, no Indian wicketkeeper had scored a Test hundred in New Zealand before Sunday. The innings also carried him past Syed Kirmani's record for the highest score by an Indian wicketkeeper in New Zealand.

What it means for the match

Pant's hundred was the acceleration inside an innings that was already a record: India's 720 for 9 is their highest Test total in New Zealand, built on Rahul's anchoring hundred a day earlier and Pant's counterattack on the fourth morning. New Zealand, resuming behind by a first-innings margin of more than 250 runs, face the rest of the fourth day and a fifth day simply to save the first Test of the series.
